results.title: CMS Policy Article A52467 - PAP devices, coding guidelines (companion to LCD L33718)
results.text:
# CPAP/PAP device coding guidelines and diagnosis requirements

## Overview

Positive airway pressure devices fall under the Durable Medical Equipment benefit category. For Medicare payment the equipment must meet the reasonable and necessary standard in the related Local Coverage Determination (L33718) and the specific statutory payment requirements.

## Diagnosis code requirements

The only diagnosis code that supports medical necessity for PAP therapy is G47.33 (obstructive sleep apnea). Having the code does not by itself guarantee coverage: the supplier must verify that all applicable coverage criteria in the LCD are met. ICD-10 codes other than G47.33 are treated as not supporting medical necessity for PAP devices, so other diagnoses cannot justify PAP claims.

results.title: CMS Transmittal 1875 - Consultation service codes no longer recognized for Medicare payment
results.text:
AI. Follow-up visits use codes 99307-99310. Nurse practitioners, clinical nurse specialists and certified nurse midwives may perform initial visits where state law permits and collaboration and supervision requirements are met. Office and outpatient: physicians and qualified nonphysician practitioners choose a new or established patient visit code (99201-99215) based on visit complexity and the patient relationship. A new patient is one who has not received professional services from the physician or physician group practice within the previous 3 years.

Critical Access Hospital Method II: appropriate new or established visit codes (99201-99215) are reported on type of bill 85X with revenue codes 96X, 97X or 98X for physicians and nonphysician practitioners with reassigned billing rights.

Rural Health Clinics and Federally Qualified Health Centers: consultation codes were discontinued in favor of office visit codes (99201-99215) and nursing facility codes (99304-99306) as appropriate.

final_text:
**Claim 38928 has a denial risk of about 10.5%.** That is below the validation-set average of 18%, and below the model's baseline of 14%. It is a carrier claim for HCPCS 96156 with principal diagnosis Z608.

**What drives the score (SHAP, log-odds):**
- **HCPCS 96156 lowers risk (×0.39 on the odds).** This is the biggest factor.
- **Line place of service code 20 raises risk (×2.0 on the odds).** This field isn't in the project's data dictionary. In the standard CMS place-of-service set, 20 is urgent care, but confirm that yourself.
- The diagnosis, billing NPI and other fields each move the score only slightly.

**What to check before submitting:**
- Confirm that place of service 20 matches where the service was actually delivered. This is the main risk-raising item.
- Confirm that 96156 and Z608 fit the documentation and the payer's rules.

The policy documents I have don't cover 96156, so I can't cite a CMS rule for it. These checks are general good practice.

**Caveat:** The denial label is synthetic. It was built from risk rules, so this score is not a real payer decision.
